dep_mix.note1: Passengers reached a cumulative 42,726,817 for January–October 2026, +55.8% versus the same period of 2023. Year-over-year growth peaked at 14.7% in March and bottomed at 4.0% in June; the latest month (October) was 11.6%.
dep_mix.note3: Growth is led by Japan and China. For January–October 2026 the two markets account for 51.6% of international departure passengers.
finds: Passengers YoY

January–October is +9.9% year over year. Monthly YoY moved between 14.7% (March, high), 4.0% (June, low) and 11.6% (October, latest). It is safer not to extend any single month’s rate into annual planning.
Japan + China share
Growth is concentrated in two markets. Japan 13.48 million (+21.3%), China 8.57 million (+22.8%). China is 3.3 times its 2023 level.
Guam / SE Asia
Southeast Asia and Guam are in decline. Guam -29.1%, Malaysia -18.1%, Thailand -16.0%, Philippines -14.4%, Vietnam -5.9%.
Europe passengers

Long-haul: Europe +8.4%, the Americas +9.2%. Fastest-growing markets above 100,000 passengers: UK +30.3%, 카자흐스탄 +27.6%, Canada +14.4%. Much of this is transit traffic — compare with the paid basis in Section 02.
Cargo YoY
Departure cargo for January–October: 1.89 million tonnes (+8.6%). Largest contributors: the Americas +9.7%, Japan +17.5%, Asia +6.1%. Cargo and flight counts do not depend on the passenger basis.
Domestic vs. 2023
Domestic January–October: 24.47 million passengers, -1.3% year over year, -9.8% versus 2023. Domestic has no transit count, so both bases match.
